The Glassblower An original passage written for LearnAce 1 The furnace in my grandfather's workshop never went out. In winter it warmed the whole street; in summer it made the air above the roof shimmer like a mirage. "Glass has a memory," he told me the first time I held a blowpipe. "Rush it, and it remembers. Cool it too fast, and one day — years later — it cracks for no reason anyone can see." 2 I was sixteen and impatient, and for months everything I made remembered my impatience. Bowls slumped. Vases split in the cooling oven overnight. He never fixed my mistakes; he only set them on a shelf by the door, where customers could see them, labelled with my name and the date. 3 I hated that shelf. I believed it was a punishment. Only years later, after he had died and I was running the shop, did I take the pieces down and line them up in order. Arranged that way, the shelf told a story — a slow correction of a lopsided rim; a gradual thinning of glass that had once been as thick as a jar. It was not a record of my failures. It was a record of my learning, kept by someone who knew I would need proof of it someday. 4 The shelf is still by the door. My own apprentice hates it, as she should. Why did the grandfather display the narrator's mistakes?
examples.answer: To create a visible record of progress over time
choices: To create a visible record of progress over time

examples.question: The Translator An original passage written for LearnAce 1 For eleven years I translated for my parents — at the bank, at the doctor's, at the parent-teacher conferences where I was, absurdly, required to relay my own report card. I learned early that translation is not a matter of swapping words. It is a matter of deciding what to leave out. 2 When the landlord said my father's English was "cute," I translated it as "He says he understands." When the doctor used the word "concerning," I said, "She wants more tests," and watched my mother's shoulders loosen. I was not lying, exactly. I was editing the world into a shape my parents could carry. 3 It took me until university to recognize that I had also been editing them. My father's jokes, which made his cousins weep with laughter, arrived in English flattened and polite. My mother's precise, sharp-edged opinions about the school system became "My mother has some questions." In my mouth, they were smaller than they were. 4 Last month my father passed his citizenship interview. He insisted on going alone. Afterward he called me, and for the first time I heard him tell a joke in English — a terrible pun about the officer's tie — and heard the officer laugh. I had spent years protecting him from a language that, it turned out, he had been quietly learning to carry himself. Why is the word "absurdly" used in paragraph 1?
examples.answer: It highlights how strange it was for a child to translate her own report card
choices: It shows the narrator disliked school
It shows the teachers were rude
It shows the conferences were funny
It highlights how strange it was for a child to translate her own report card

examples.question: The Glassblower An original passage written for LearnAce 1 The furnace in my grandfather's workshop never went out. In winter it warmed the whole street; in summer it made the air above the roof shimmer like a mirage. "Glass has a memory," he told me the first time I held a blowpipe. "Rush it, and it remembers. Cool it too fast, and one day — years later — it cracks for no reason anyone can see." 2 I was sixteen and impatient, and for months everything I made remembered my impatience. Bowls slumped. Vases split in the cooling oven overnight. He never fixed my mistakes; he only set them on a shelf by the door, where customers could see them, labelled with my name and the date. 3 I hated that shelf. I believed it was a punishment. Only years later, after he had died and I was running the shop, did I take the pieces down and line them up in order. Arranged that way, the shelf told a story — a slow correction of a lopsided rim; a gradual thinning of glass that had once been as thick as a jar. It was not a record of my failures. It was a record of my learning, kept by someone who knew I would need proof of it someday. 4 The shelf is still by the door. My own apprentice hates it, as she should.
